findings.title: One failed SendGrid cancel stops the whole cancel batch, and the earlier rows are never deleted
findings.body:
The `try` wraps the whole `for` loop. If `client.request` throws for any reminder, the loop stops and `Promise.all(workflowRemindersToDelete)` (line 74) never runs. The `prisma.workflowReminder.delete(...)` calls pushed into it are lazy PrismaPromises, so they never execute either. The batches already cancelled at SendGrid keep `cancelled: true` in the DB. On the next run (every 15 min, `.github/workflows/cron-scheduleEmailReminders.yml:8`) the cron POSTs `cancel` again for those same batch IDs. That likely fails because the batch already has a status (SendGrid expects PATCH for that). The loop then aborts at the same place each time, so every cancelled reminder later in the list is never cancelled and gets sent to attendees of cancelled bookings, with only a `console.log`.

The duplicate-cancel case also happens on its own. `requestReschedule` marks the reminders `cancelled: true` (bookings.tsx:490). When the attendee then rebooks, `handleNewBooking` loads the original booking, including CANCELLED status (handleNewBooking.ts:750, 772), and cancels the same batch immediately (handleNewBooking.ts:968). The `immediateDelete` branch neither deletes the row nor clears `cancelled` (emailReminderManager.ts:213-223), so the cron later cancels that batch a second time.

Fix: put a try/catch around each reminder, and await the delete inside the loop. Also have the `immediateDelete` branch delete the row (or clear `cancelled`) after the SendGrid cancel succeeds.

findings.title: Late cancellations can still send the reminder because the cancel waits for the cron
findings.body: Booking cancellation, request-reschedule, edited steps and removed event types no longer cancel the SendGrid batch. They only set `cancelled: true`, and the 15‑minute cron cancels reminders due within the next hour (scheduleEmailReminders.ts:44-51). If a booking is cancelled less than about 15 minutes before a scheduled reminder, the cron either runs too late or first hits the `deleteMany` for past reminders (scheduleEmailReminders.ts:34-41). The attendee then gets a reminder for a meeting that was cancelled. Before this change the cancel was sent to SendGrid immediately. Consider cancelling immediately when `scheduledDate` is within the cron interval plus SendGrid's cancel lead time, and deferring only reminders further out.

findings.title: try/catch around fire-and-forget async calls catches nothing
findings.body: `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` are async and are called inside `forEach` without `await`. A rejection would never reach this `catch`, so `log.error` here can never run. Both functions already catch their own errors. Drop the try/catch, or collect the promises and `await Promise.allSettled(...)` so the cancels finish before the request returns.

findings.title: Reminder DB updates are no longer awaited before the response
findings.body: Before this change the reminder `deleteMany` calls were added to `prismaPromises` and awaited at line 497. Now `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` and `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` (which do the DB update or delete) are started but never awaited. If the serverless function is frozen after it responds, a reminder may never be marked `cancelled`, and its email is then sent. The same applies in bookings.tsx:488-494 and the workflows.tsx update paths. Consider collecting the returned promises and awaiting them with the other `prismaPromises`.

summary: The PR stops cancelling SendGrid batches right away. Most paths now set the new `cancelled` flag, and the email cron cancels flagged reminders due within the next hour. Reschedules, deleted steps and deleted workflows still cancel immediately. Two things to fix: (1) In the cron, a single `try` wraps the whole cancel loop and the row deletes are lazy. One failed SendGrid cancel therefore aborts the loop, leaves already-cancelled rows flagged, and makes the next runs re-cancel them and fail again. That happens in practice after a request-reschedule followed by the rebooking, because the immediate cancel in `handleNewBooking` leaves the rows flagged. (2) Cancellations made less than about one cron interval before a reminder can no longer stop it. Smaller points: the try/catch in `handleNewBooking` can never catch anything, and the reminder DB updates are no longer awaited before the response. The `WorkflowStepContainer` change keeps the sender field visible.
